item.title: SCP IDEA: "Home": Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Yes, but what does nostalgia have to do with Sarkicism, then? Now it's moving in a different direction of horror, which is at odds with your feelings of being calm / at ease.

Ideally, whatever you add to the concept needs to link together. So, for example, is there another entity / reason why these people are being kept in the village against their will?

e.g. Is there like the spirit of a small child who lost her parents to a fire long ago, and now casts a spell on anyone who enters so that they will never leave her again?

Have a reason for your anomaly. It doesn't have to be spelt out in the actual article, but you as the author need to know it.

item.title: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight: Re: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback.

why dragons? I don't really have a reason for the fact that they're dragons, I guess I'm kinda using it as a placeholder, since I had been happening to be drawing a dragon creature when I came up with the SCP idea. I like your suggestion though, maybe they don't have a physical form that we can see since they're from another dimension, and take the form of children when they enter our world so they can take people? as for why they are abducting people, I feel like leaving it unanswered is better, it gives the article some more mystery and gives the reader something to think about.

For the being trapped by the house part, the idea is still a little half baked rn. So I'm thinking that an outside party (maybe a GOI? Maybe another SCP entirely?) built the structure to contain them, but they didn't do it properly so the creatures can still get out a certain distance, like there's some magic thing about the house that traps them, but it's not strong enough so they can still go outside. But I'm not sure how to explain how the Foundation would figure out this information.

If I could make the idea work, I think I would do something like a dimensional rift opened and these creatures started pouring out of it so the house was built to contain the rift, but the rift was so unstable that it keeps teleporting around. And maybe the reason they're abducting people is for a ritual of some kind to break the house's trap? I don't really have anything yet for that idea, but it seems kinda tacky anyway so I'd rather leave the reason they abduct people a mystery

Honestly, I might just scrap the whole 1km limit thing, unless you think the idea I laid out here is worth trying to flesh out.

item.title: The Phantom: Re: The Phantom
item.content:encoded:
If this thing has supposedly "superior intelligence", then why not try and cut a deal with The Foundation to help its mission? It has to realize that with the resources of The Foundation backing it, it would be a lot easier to accomplish its mission, both in terms of finding suitable victims as well as providing protection on the way to its eventual goal.

The Foundation has no problems killing people if the means justify the ends; if they know that the deaths prevent a cataclysm, they would likely support the being.

Also, you need to delineate the specific cataclysm. A generic cataclysm doesn't inspire horror like a specific one does. So have some fun with it.

Lastly, give us some details on the GOI. While you can get away some generality, at least mention if it's an evil cult, some businessmen with philanthropic ideals, or even a human-sacrificing cult with philanthropic ideals. Just something would help here.

item.title: Scp idea give away: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post

Where should I post ideas?

Generally it's discouraged to just leave ideas and expect others to write them up, because that invites turning the forum into a dumping ground and encourages laziness. If you feel like your idea is something people would really be interested in, you can post it in the Foundation Universe forum or ask in Questions Desk if anyone would be willing to co-author with you.

I looked at the ideas forum requirements and didn’t mention not being able to post concepts.

Given the name of the forum, it's expected to be self-explanatory that the forum is for seeking critique on ideas.

item.title: De Facto: Re: De Facto

I've just clarified the ambiguity of its knowledge and containment. It's uncontainable, but efforts can be made to effectively minimize the number of victims by tracking it through what path it appears to be taking based areas previously affected by its anomalous properties.

item.title: New SCP. Der Verlorene: Re: New SCP. Der Verlorene
item.content:encoded:
The problem is that seems to be just a single instance of a shellshocked soldier. With that as a given, there's little of interest here. You need to build more into the character than that; if he could be treated then he may give some interesting historical notes, even possibly describe the SCP that transported him through time.

Or he could have the ability to time travel himself, and the ability was triggered due to stress. even if it was a one-time ability, it could be fascinating to study him. If it's not, then he could be of help in exploring historical eras, possibly confirming details.

If you are going to keep him shellshocked, then you need to show what he can add to the knowledge of The Foundation. There has to be some sign of what caused him to time travel or it's just a neat idea.

In what seems to be a common theme today, this is just the beginning of an idea, and needs to be fleshed out somewhat or it's just The Foundation equivalent of a freak; he's going to be confined until he dies, possibly gets killed, and not really contribute anything.

item.title: Seeking review: Furry Clinic.: Seeking review: Furry Clinic.
item.content:encoded:
A bullied person makes a clinic that turns people into their fursona counterparts, permanantly, and painfully, you won't be able to mingle in society.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Alright I think I can write a decent article this time, this would be my 5th attempt at a concept being approved, although I thought of many more I scrapped. So, yeah, a furry, gets bullied in his childhood so he decides to become a furry, and thinks that: "Every furry I know wants to be their character! I'll find a way to make this come true!" He experiments a while to finally make a clinic which anyone who enters comes out their fursona. Non-furries find it exceptionally hard to locate. Now a side affect of this surgery is well, the subjects immediately seek out the nearest furry, and try to force them in, once they do so, the subject will return to the place they last slept, and wake up with no memory of this, I intended to make the creator of the clinic realize what he had done, he had ripped families apart, because he thought he was helping them, in reality, he didn't.

item.title: The Railyard To Everywhere: Re: The Railyard To Everywhere
item.content:encoded:
This is not a bad idea, and has a lot of great detail. However, the biggest problem is that the intelligence that set this up is not even hinted at, no trademarks, company signage, or anything like that. This sounds like something that was expensive to create and maintain, and that requires some sort of intelligence, even if it's just company of some sort.

Basically, whoever set it up needs to be defined and given some explanation here.

Also, if there needs to be some form of security. If they can't control who comes in, they can control what people do there. Even if it's just an old man with a whistle, if they are worried enough about there cargo that they are willing to kill for it, then it makes no sense to not have some form of security.

Lastly, you may want to consider who they are doing business with. There is no such thing as a stop that's just a stop; why is there a junction on Earth, and who are they doing business with here? Even if they are restocking, how are they doing that?

Good skeleton; now flesh it out.

item.title: SCP-5832: Re: SCP-5832
item.content:encoded:
1) You don't need to make it an SCP; once it demonstrates anomalous attributes it's a given. Also, it feels that this has not been greenlighted but it already has a number.

2) The Red Paper Castle: It may be better to phrase it such that the red paper was transformed into a duplicate of the original castle. I know it's semantics, but it just feels better. You may want to go through and look for similar instances; there are a number of similarly bulky phrasing.

3) This is a good start, but it needs to be expanded upon. Do they have a history? Why did they automatically become enemies, with no apparent attempt at diplomacy? Where are they getting more paper to build the castle? If I put a pack of white paper near the castle, what would happen? Did they have a religion prior to the researcher? What form does that worship take?

Heck, what's the psychology of the castle dwellers? Is it based off real medieval people or an idealized form, such as the SCA? For that matter, why was it built in the first place, was it for a warg game or just to see what could happen?

Again, really cool start. Now flesh it out.

2) If you are going to make this the first, then you may want to include a way for it to be neutralized, and not just temporarily. Also, no fear of death is likely to create an SCP that is going to be a lot rougher and therefore be harder to contain. The GOI in question may have actually been in the right.

If there does seem to be more of these, then it's possible that The Foundation may assign an MTF or two if they become a major problem.

3) If the phantom simply possesses another car then there is no reason for the memories to carry over; it's the same entity so it would have the same memories. If the phantom died or there was some sort of hive mentality I could see a reason for the note, but since it's not a reincarnation, a new phantom. or otherwise a new entity there's no reason for the note.

item.title: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.content:encoded:
A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Edit: Added the required template.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Page starts with basic containment procedures and a description. The main part of the narrative will be in the experiment log, which will reveal more about the effects of the SCP and may include interview logs with the test subjects.

Elevator Pitch: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is a weight loss pill that you can order a subscription to though an anomalous phone number. Each pill rewrites your memories a little bit to make you believe you lost weight after taking the pill. Since it does not actually cause weight loss in the present, you probably will actually gain weight without knowing it. The more pills that are taken the fatter you will believe you used to be and the further back in time it changes your memories. Eventually, you will be convinced that you have been morbidly obese your entire life before you started taking the pills. If you keep taking the pills past this point (I will call this the critical point for now), things start to get strange. The boxes that the pills come in have two languages on them. One is English (or whatever language you speak) and is all lies, and the other is an unknown language. After the critical point, you gain the ability to read the unknown language, which tells the truth about what the pills do, and you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a weight loss pill that retroactively turns users into gluttony monsters in human form, or at least makes them think they are.

Additional Notes: I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories or physical records like pictures. I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not. I may end up leaving it ambiguous if it is actually changing the past or just your memories.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
